title: E2E smoke for the bundled stack
description: A CI job that brings up the full packaged deployment with the tournament profile on, from published images, and checks the path a club would take: enable tournaments, see provisioning succeed, open TMX and sign in, create a tournament, see it on the public pages and in the app's home page after sync.

recommended_model.name: Sonnet 5.5
recommended_model.rationale: Test authoring over a defined happy path.

acceptance_criteria: A scheduled and on-release CI job runs the packaged stack end to end with tournaments on
Covers provisioning, TMX sign-in, tournament creation, public page visibility and app sync
Also runs once with the profile off to confirm no tournament links appear
Failures upload container logs and Playwright traces

notes: See docs/courthive_bundle_design.md (rewritten 2026-11-22 for latest upstream): sign-in to TMX is by the hand-over; internal/courthive/integration_test.go and the two-hostname test stack show the shape. The CI job needs published images.

testing_requirements: The job itself, green on two consecutive runs

context.user_story: As the maintainer, I want to know each release's tournament bundle actually works.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
